title: Joining theories: common languages and consistent pairs
summary: Build a joint model of two theories when their common language contains no sentence separating them.
abstract: Two consistent theories can become inconsistent when combined: one may require exactly one object while the other requires two distinct objects. Their common language already expresses that disagreement, even when they share no relation or function symbols. We prove a converse for theories in finite vocabularies. If no sentence in their common language follows from one theory while its negation follows from the other, they have a joint model. The construction adds the same fresh names on both sides and decides statements while preserving this stronger compatibility condition. Every element of the resulting term models has a shared name, which lets us identify their common parts and combine their interpretations. This supplies the model construction used to prove first-order interpolation.
